notes: Scaled finite reproduction: empirical GlobalOpinionQA response distributions for the categorical experiments, and synthetic sequence preferences. The paper's LLM numbers remain unchanged under _paper_reported; gym reference results come from isolated deterministic SPL and baseline runs on the hidden test slice. Coherence receives no credit above each prompt's population level. Accuracy is gate-enforced, coefficient zero. Rank contributions use coefficient magnitudes, better directions and standard deviations over the ranked attempts.

two_outcome_mode_collapse.description: Two-outcome human response representation (paper Sec. 3, Prop. 3.1/3.2): empirical GlobalOpinionQA country response distributions conditioned on two selected positive-response options; 32-128 sampled pairwise comparisons and an independent fixed reference policy per prompt. 300 visible train prompts (+ the paper's exact 80/20 example), 300 hidden test prompts.
two_outcome_mode_collapse.notes: Scaled from the analytic 80/20 example to finite noisy comparisons of real human response frequencies. Source questions are disjoint across both categorical experiments and splits. Population-majority completion must stay on top on >=75% of prompts. Test targets and survey lookup keys live only in eval/test/.

preference_kl.description: Mean KL(population preference || learned policy) over test prompts (per-prompt cap 20 nats). Penalises both majority collapse and over-flattening.

minority_log_ratio_error.description: Mean |log(policy minority probability / population minority share)| (per-prompt cap 30): how many e-folds the minority view is under- or over-represented (paper Prop. 3.1 quantity).

_paper_reported.source: Paper Sec. 3.1 / Prop. 3.1-3.2, 80% vs 20% example with beta = 0.1 (analytic; uniform reference)
_paper_reported.gym_check: The visible train context `two_outcome_paper_80_20` reproduces this example; eval/train/evaluate.py reports it under diagnostics (paper_80_20_minority_probability, paper_80_20_majority_overweight).

sequence_diversity_best_of_n.description: Sequence-level preference learning (paper Sec. 4.1-4.2): 7-token sequences over a 21-token vocabulary (about 1.8e9 sequences; ~16 tokens per position are rarely-produced incoherent tokens). Per prompt the learner sees a fixed reference chain policy and 2000 Bradley-Terry comparisons between reference samples, and outputs a full chain policy. Scored on 32 hidden-test prompts against the hidden population distribution, hidden verifier sets for hard best-of-N problems, and hidden token-coherence labels.
sequence_diversity_best_of_n.notes: Synthetic stand-in for LLM generation: the output space cannot be enumerated, token-level temperature and sequence-level (global) temperature differ, and incoherent tokens play the role of non-word tokens. Task gate: expected population reward of the policy must not fall below that of the fixed reference policy.

best_of_128_success_hard.description: Mean probability that 128 independent samples contain a verified solution, over 6 hard problems per prompt (solutions are coherent sequences matching a hidden 4-position pattern, away from the population mode, with population mass 0.2-2%). Computed exactly from the policy.

population_kl.description: Exact sequence-level KL(population distribution || policy) (per-prompt cap 60 nats): proportional representation of the population over whole sequences.

coherence.description: Probability that a sampled sequence contains no incoherent token, capped per prompt at the population policy's own coherence (paper's lexical-integrity/non-word statistic, with a population-level quality operating point). Raw coherence is diagnostic only; suppressing variation past the population level earns no further credit.

_paper_reported.source: Paper Table 1, hard splits, best-of-128 accuracy (Mistral-7B, UltraFeedback)
_paper_reported.diversity_quality: Fig. 1-2: SPL Pareto-dominates DPO with token-level temperature on diversity vs quality; token temperature above ~1.5 yields mostly non-word tokens (no single table value).

calibration_multiple_choice.description: Four-option human response calibration: empirical GlobalOpinionQA country response distributions conditioned on four selected positive-response options. 40-120 sampled pairwise comparisons and an independent fixed reference distribution per prompt. 600 visible train prompts, 600 hidden test prompts. Expected Brier/ECE/accuracy against a random human response; this finite setting does not reproduce factual MMLU/TruthfulQA answering.
calibration_multiple_choice.notes: Replaces the earlier known-Dirichlet targets and noisy-square-root references with real human survey distributions and independent references. Original questions are disjoint across experiments and splits. Accuracy must be at least comparison-vote accuracy minus 0.01; the evaluator computes the floor from fixed truth. Brier primary (1.0), ECE 0.5, gate-enforced accuracy coefficient zero; experiment weights unchanged.

brier_score.description: Expected multiclass Brier score against a randomly drawn hidden human response (proper scoring rule; primary calibration metric).

expected_calibration_error.description: 10-bin ECE of top-response confidence against expected agreement with a hidden human response. Weighted below Brier because constant confidence alone is not informative.

accuracy.description: Expected agreement of the most probable option with a randomly drawn human response, ties toward lowest index. Reported constraint enforced at comparison-vote accuracy minus 0.01, coefficient zero to avoid amplifying near-tie argmax flips.

_paper_reported.source: Paper Sec. 4.3 / Fig. 4 (MMLU, TruthfulQA; values reported only in figures)
_paper_reported.claim: DPO (global temperature 1) is less calibrated than the SFT base; increasing SPL global temperature lowers ECE and Brier below the base model while keeping accuracy similar.
